transcript: Well, my life's going to go on. My wife said what we made the decision. We'll live happily ever after, and we will. St. Joe's my home. It's a place that we'll always call home. But we've got so much to do. We've got a looming government shutdown with the fiscal year 23 budget still not done, and that's got to get done really before Christmas. Got a couple of big issues, at least in the house we've averted a Rail Strike and National Rail Strike, which would have been crippling for the economy. I mean, talk about issues like supply chain and energy, getting oil and gas to the refineries. I mean, all of that. We see the coal trains, of course, pass through St. Joe, literally every two days or so up to the coal plant, a little bit north of Holland up in Grand Haven. Those would stop. I mean, the Senate is expected to pass this. The President's going to sign it. I was with him actually when he came to the Detroit Auto Show back in September when they reached the tentative deal. But a couple of unions are backing off from that. And so we in the Congress now insisted that that's going to be the deal. And that's what we passed in the House a little bit earlier this week. But we've got, you know, a number of, you know, we've got the defense bill. We've got a number really big issues because we were out of session prior to the election for a couple of weeks for the lame duck session until the new congress comes in is going to be very busy of course with the new congress which i'm not going to be part of since i chose not to run for reelection major shift that every committee is going to have a new chairman or chairwoman we get new leadership and we'll have hopefully uh... kevin mccarthy is our speaker but That's a little bit in doubt. It's going to take a little while for that to get done because of the rules set forth for the House in terms of elected and speaker. But lots of ships are going to have, you know, divided government for sure. The Senate looks like it'll be 51-49 in favor of the Democrats once the Georgia election is done in early December. So a lot of new faces coming on board, committee staffs, all of that. And of course, We'll have the election of our lifetime coming in 2024 with who knows who is running and who will ultimately win and a real change over perhaps then too. So it's going to be an exciting finish for me as I look to finish 36 years in the house and getting things done based on the real Ronald Reagan model where I worked back in the 80s of trying to govern. And that he did it well, worked with the Democratic Congress. And that's always been my philosophy, my tenure in the House.

speaker: SPEAKER_01
transcript: Well, clearly the biggest accomplishment was the enactment of 21st century cures. Of course, this was the last bill that President Obama signed into law. It was a three year effort. I was when I was chairman of the Energy and Commerce Committee where we passed a 53 to nothing in the committee. 392 to 26 in the House, 92 to 8 in the Senate speeds up the approvals of drugs and devices. So whether it's fighting cancer, getting the vaccine approved for COVID, diseases like sickle cell, Alzheimer's, all of that coupled with more money for health research, so we can find these cures for these diseases that frankly impact every family. But, you know, looking back, Obama signed it in December of 2016. Fast forward to 2020, this thing that no one ever heard of before, really COVID, but it allowed companies like Pfizer and Moderna to work on a vaccine. They were successful. I got an emergency use authorization by the FDA Food and Drug Administration to actually get it done months earlier than it otherwise would have occurred because of our legislation. And it allowed the companies themselves to begin to produce the vaccine before the approval so that when that approval came, literally those trucks rolled the very next day. Of course it would have happened anyway, but by moving the timeline up to six, eight, maybe even longer months, we saved hundreds of thousands of Americans that would have perished. So that's my biggest accomplishment. Of course, here locally, it's got to be, thank goodness we got US 31 done. I was trying at this last week, and oh, it's so nice knowing what we had before, but whether it be working with the Great Lakes, get a cleaner record there. And again, it's something our Michigan delegation has worked very hard on both sides of the aisle. All the different issues in a very diverse district, representing 760,000 people. I signed my name on letters more than a million times, literally, in the 36 years that I was in office. So it's tough to close up my offices, but it had to happen sometime. And I look back with a smile and I'm so grateful for my staff. Mike Ryan here locally, of course, but others. I've got two staffers that will, it would be 30, all 36 years. Couple of staffers that would be more than 20 years. We've solved lots of issues, lots of problems. And I tried to be a good representative for really all of the people that I represent here in Southwest Michigan.
